text:
Delivery Items are the linen/fabric items that a hotel has requested and that the driver is
expected to deliver during a hotel visit.
A delivery item has:
- Expected Quantity — quantity requested by the hotel/order.
- Delivered Quantity — actual quantity handed over to the hotel.
- Return Fresh — fresh linen from the expected quantity that was not delivered.

A Regular Order is a recurring hotel order.
Regular Orders can be:
- Daily
- Weekly
- Monthly
The exact delivery items depend on the hotel's order.
Most hotels use the same/common types of linen for their orders.

Expected Quantity is the quantity of a particular linen item that the hotel/order requires.
Example:
- Expected Quantity = 500
- The driver is expected to deliver 500 units.
The Expected Quantity is the reference quantity used to determine whether there is a delivery
shortage.
Delivered Quantity is the actual quantity of fresh linen handed over to the hotel.

If:
- Expected = 500
- Delivered = 500
Then there is no shortage and Return Fresh is not required.

If:
- Expected = 500
- Delivered = 450
Then:
- Delivered = 450
- Return Fresh = 50
The app requires the Return Fresh quantity to be entered before proceeding.

section: 5. Delivery Quantity Rules — Driver cannot over-deliver
text:
The driver cannot deliver more than the Expected Quantity.
The app prevents Delivered Quantity from being greater than Expected Quantity.
Example:
- Expected = 500
- Driver has 520 available
The driver can deliver only 500.
The extra 20 units cannot be entered as Delivered Quantity.

Return Fresh represents fresh linen that was expected but was not delivered to the hotel.
Return Fresh is calculated as:
Return Fresh = Expected Quantity − Delivered Quantity
Example:
- Expected = 500
- Delivered = 450
- Return Fresh = 50
The driver should enter 50 as Return Fresh.

section: 6. Return Fresh — Return Fresh cannot exceed Expected Quantity
text:
The app prevents Return Fresh from being greater than Expected Quantity.
Example:
- Expected = 500
- Return Fresh cannot be 501.

section: 6. Return Fresh — Return Fresh is required for shortages
text:
If Delivered Quantity is less than Expected Quantity, Return Fresh must be entered.
The app blocks the driver from continuing until the required Return Fresh quantities have been
entered.
This applies even when the shortage is only 1 unit.
Example:
- Expected = 500
- Delivered = 499
- Return Fresh = 1
The driver must enter the Return Fresh quantity before continuing.

section: 6. Return Fresh — Return Fresh can be zero
text:
Return Fresh can be 0.
When there is no shortage:
- Expected = 500
- Delivered = 500
- Return Fresh = 0

Return Fresh is entered separately for each delivery item/product that has a shortage.
Example:
Item

Each short product requires its own Return Fresh quantity.

| Item | Expected | Delivered | Return Fresh |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bedsheet | 500 | 450 | 50 |
| Pillow Cover | 300 | 280 | 20 |

When the delivered quantity is less than the expected quantity:
1.​ Enter the actual Delivered Quantity.
2.​ Enter Return Fresh.
3.​ Complete the remaining hotel visit information.
4.​ Continue to Pickup / Heavy Soil / Damaged / Remarks as applicable.
5.​ Save and Continue.
6.​ Select the applicable Shortage Reason.
7.​ Generate the Digital DC.

section: 9. Return Fresh and Shortage Reason Are Different
text:
Return Fresh records how many fresh linen units were not delivered.
Shortage Reason records why the expected quantity was not delivered.
Example:
Expected = 500​
Delivered = 450​
Return Fresh = 50
The driver then selects the appropriate shortage reason, such as:
- Customer Refused
- Packed Less
- Damaged in Transit
- Soiled Quantity Less
- Other
Return Fresh is therefore a quantity, while Shortage Reason is the reason for the shortage.

section: 10. Hotel Refuses Part of the Delivery
text:
If the hotel refuses part of the expected quantity:
Example:
- Expected = 500
- Hotel accepts = 450
- Return Fresh = 50
- Shortage Reason = Customer Refused
The driver delivers only the accepted quantity and records the remaining quantity as Return
Fresh.

If fresh linen is damaged while being transported from the warehouse to the hotel:
Example:
- Expected = 500
- 20 fresh units are damaged during transit.
- Good units delivered = 480
- Return Fresh = 20
- Shortage Reason = Damaged in Transit
The damaged fresh linen is returned to the warehouse.
Damaged in Transit refers to fresh linen damaged during transportation.
This is different from Damaged recorded during Pickup, which refers to physical damage in
used linen returned by the hotel.

If the warehouse has packed more than the expected quantity, the driver can still deliver only
the Expected Quantity.
Example:
- Expected = 500
- Warehouse packed = 520
- Driver can deliver = 500
The driver cannot enter 520 as Delivered Quantity.

section: 13. Return Fresh Editing Rules — Before Save and Continue
text: Return Fresh can be edited before Save and Continue.

section: 13. Return Fresh Editing Rules — After DC Generation but Before OTP
text:
Return Fresh can be changed after the Digital DC has been generated, as long as the DC has
not yet been OTP authenticated.
If the quantity is changed:
- Update the quantity.
- Regenerate the DC.
- Complete the new authentication flow.

section: 13. Return Fresh Editing Rules — After OTP Authentication
text:
Return Fresh cannot be changed after OTP authentication.
The OTP-authenticated DC is final.

The app enforces the delivery quantity rules.
The app prevents:
- Delivered Quantity > Expected Quantity
- Return Fresh > Expected Quantity
The app also blocks progression when a required Return Fresh quantity has not been entered.

Expected = 500​
Delivered = 500​
Return Fresh = 0
Result: No shortage.

Expected = 500​
Delivered = 499​
Return Fresh = 1
Result: Return Fresh must be entered.

section: 15. Important Examples — Example 3 — Customer refuses quantity
text:
Expected = 500​
Delivered = 450​
Return Fresh = 50​
Shortage Reason = Customer Refused

Expected = 500​
Delivered = 480​
Return Fresh = 20​
Shortage Reason = Damaged in Transit
Damaged fresh linen is returned to the warehouse.

section: 15. Important Examples — Example 5 — Warehouse has extra stock
text:
Expected = 500​
Warehouse packed = 520​
Delivered = 500
The driver cannot deliver more than 500.

section: 16. FAQ — Can the driver deliver more than the Expected Quantity?​
text: No. The app prevents Delivered Quantity from exceeding Expected Quantity.
Return Fresh is the quantity of expected fresh linen that was not delivered.

section: 16. FAQ — How is Return Fresh calculated?​
text: Return Fresh = Expected Quantity − Delivered Quantity.

section: 16. FAQ — Can Return Fresh be greater than Expected Quantity?​
text: No. The app prevents this.

section: 16. FAQ — Is Return Fresh required for every shortage?​
text: Yes. Even a 1-unit shortage requires Return Fresh to be entered.
Yes.

section: 16. FAQ — Can Return Fresh be edited before Save and Continue?​
text: Yes.

section: 16. FAQ — Can Return Fresh be changed after DC generation?​
text: Yes, if the DC has not yet been OTP authenticated. The DC must be regenerated.

section: 16. FAQ — Can Return Fresh be changed after OTP authentication?​
text: No.

section: 16. FAQ — What happens if the hotel refuses part of the delivery?​
text:
Deliver the accepted quantity, enter the refused quantity as Return Fresh, and select Customer
Refused as the shortage reason.

section: 16. FAQ — What happens when fresh linen is damaged during transportation?​
text:
Deliver the good quantity, enter the damaged quantity as Return Fresh, select Damaged in
Transit, and return the damaged fresh linen to the warehouse.

DC means Delivery Challan.
A Digital DC is an automatically generated document containing the delivery and pickup
information entered by the driver in the Pushpak app.
The Digital DC acts as proof of delivery.
The Digital DC maintains transparency between the driver, packer, hotel, and company.
The Digital DC records:
- Delivered quantities
- Return Fresh quantities
- Pickup quantities
- Heavy Soil quantities
- Damaged quantities
The driver does not manually type the Digital DC.

Pushpak currently uses Digital DC.
Current process:
1.​ Driver enters delivery quantities.
2.​ Driver enters Return Fresh quantities when applicable.
3.​ Driver enters pickup quantities.
4.​ Driver enters Heavy Soil and Damaged quantities when applicable.
5.​ Driver enters Remarks.
6.​ Driver taps Save and Continue.
7.​ If delivery is short, driver selects a Shortage Reason.
8.​ Driver taps Generate DC.
9.​ Pushpak automatically generates the Digital DC from the entered quantities.
10.​Driver reviews the DC.
11.​Hotel authenticates the DC using OTP.
12.​Successful OTP authentication marks the delivery as accepted.

The old process used a physical paper challan.
Old process:
1.​ Driver writes the challan by hand on physical paper.
2.​ Driver photographs the paper challan using the app camera.
3.​ Driver uploads the photograph.
4.​ App automatically detects quantities from the photograph using OCR.
Problems with the old process:
- Handwriting could be unclear.
- OCR could misread quantities.
- Driver had to write the challan.
- Driver had to photograph the challan.
- Driver had to upload the photograph.
- Paper could be lost, damaged, or smudged.
- Detection errors could require correction.
The Digital DC removes the paper and OCR steps.

DC generation is the final step of the hotel visit before hotel authentication.
The driver cannot generate the DC until the required delivery and pickup information is
complete.
If the delivery quantity is short, the driver must select a Shortage Reason before generating the
DC.
DC generation flow:
Delivery entries → Pickup entries → Save and Continue → Shortage Reason if applicable →
Generate DC → Review DC → OTP Authentication.

The Digital DC automatically uses information already entered in the Pushpak app.
The driver does not manually enter quantities into the DC.
The Digital DC can contain:
- Delivered quantity
- Return Fresh quantity
- Pickup quantity
- Heavy Soil quantity
- Damaged quantity
Example:
If the driver enters:
- Delivery = 500 bath towels
- Return Fresh = 20 bath towels
- Pickup = 480 bath towels
- Heavy Soil = 5 bath towels
- Damaged = 3 bath towels
The Digital DC automatically contains those quantities.

1.​ Complete delivery entries.
2.​ Complete Return Fresh entries if applicable.
3.​ Complete pickup entries.
4.​ Complete Heavy Soil and Damaged entries if applicable.
5.​ Enter Remarks.
6.​ Tap Save and Continue.
7.​ Select Shortage Reason if delivery quantity is short.
8.​ Tap Generate DC.
9.​ Review the automatically generated Digital DC.

After the Digital DC is generated, the driver must authenticate it with the hotel using OTP.
OTP authentication steps:
1.​ Review the Digital DC.
2.​ Tap Authenticate DC.
3.​ A list of authorized hotel contacts appears.
4.​ Select the hotel person who will authenticate the DC.
5.​ Tap Send OTP.
6.​ The selected hotel person receives the OTP on their registered phone number.
7.​ Ask the hotel person for the OTP.
8.​ Enter the OTP in Pushpak.
9.​ DC authentication succeeds.
10.​Delivery is marked successful.
The OTP is sent to the selected hotel person, not to the driver.

The driver can select another person from the authorized hotel contact list if the initially intended
hotel person is unavailable.
The driver does not have to use only one specific hotel person if another authorized person is
available in the list.

If the driver enters the wrong OTP, the driver can try again.
If OTP authentication repeatedly fails, the driver should contact the team.
If the hotel person refuses to provide the OTP, the driver should contact the team.

If the driver changes quantities after generating the DC but before OTP authentication:
1.​ Edit the incorrect quantity.
2.​ Generate the DC again.
3.​ A new DC is created.
4.​ Authenticate the new DC.
5.​ Send a new OTP.
6.​ Enter the new OTP.
A regenerated DC requires a new OTP.
The previous OTP cannot be used for the regenerated DC.

If the driver notices an incorrect quantity before generating the DC, the driver can edit the
quantity.
The driver should correct the quantity before generating the DC.

If the driver notices an incorrect quantity after generating the DC but before OTP authentication,
the driver can edit the quantity and regenerate the DC.
The regenerated DC must be authenticated again.
A new OTP is required for the regenerated DC.

Once the DC has been successfully authenticated using OTP, the DC cannot be changed.
The driver must make corrections before successful OTP authentication.

Successful OTP authentication means:
- Hotel has accepted the delivery.
- DC is a verified record.
- Delivery is marked successful.
- Hotel visit is completed.
- The authenticated DC cannot be changed.
The hotel receives a copy of the Digital DC.

The driver cannot proceed to the next hotel until the DC has been authenticated.
DC authentication is required to complete the hotel visit.

If delivered quantity is less than expected quantity:
1.​ Driver enters the actual delivery quantity.
2.​ Driver taps Save and Continue.
3.​ Driver selects the applicable Shortage Reason.
4.​ Driver generates the Digital DC.
5.​ The DC contains the entered delivery information.

Remarks are part of the hotel visit flow.
The driver enters Remarks before generating the DC.

- DC = Delivery Challan.
- Digital DC is automatically generated from driver-entered quantities.
- Driver does not manually type the DC.
- Old process used a handwritten physical challan and OCR.
- Current process does not require a physical paper challan.
- Current process does not require OCR.
- DC is generated after required delivery and pickup information is entered.
- Shortage Reason is required when delivery quantity is short.
- Hotel authentication is required before completing the visit.
- OTP is sent to the selected authorized hotel person's registered phone number.
- Driver can select another authorized hotel person if the first person is unavailable.
- Wrong OTP can be tried again.
- Repeated OTP failure requires contacting the team.
- Hotel refusal to provide OTP requires contacting the team.
- Editing is possible before OTP authentication.
- Regenerating a DC requires a new OTP.
- Old OTP cannot authenticate a regenerated DC.
- DC cannot be changed after successful OTP authentication.
- Driver cannot proceed to the next hotel until DC authentication is complete.
- Hotel receives a copy of the Digital DC.
DC means Delivery Challan.

A Digital DC is an automatically generated Delivery Challan created from quantities entered in
the Pushpak app.

section: Do I manually enter the DC?
text: No. The Digital DC automatically uses the quantities entered in the app.

section: What was the old DC process?
text:
The driver wrote a physical challan by hand, photographed it, uploaded it, and the app used
OCR to detect the quantities.

section: Do I need paper for the Digital DC?
text: No. The Digital DC does not require a physical paper challan.

section: Do I need to scan the challan?
text: No. The current Digital DC process does not use OCR or paper scanning.

section: When do I generate the DC?
text:
Generate the DC after completing the required delivery and pickup entries and selecting a
Shortage Reason when applicable.
The selected authorized hotel person receives the OTP on their registered phone number.

section: Can I select another hotel person?
text:
Yes. If the intended person is unavailable, the driver can select another person from the
authorized list.

section: What if the hotel person refuses to give me the OTP?
text: Contact the team.

section: What if I enter the wrong OTP?
text: You can try again.

section: What if OTP verification keeps failing?
text: Contact the team.

section: What if I enter the wrong quantity before generating the DC?
text: You can edit the quantity before generating the DC.

section: What if I enter the wrong quantity after generating the DC?
text: If OTP authentication has not happened, edit the quantity and regenerate the DC.

section: Do I need a new OTP after regenerating the DC?
text: Yes. A regenerated DC requires a new OTP.

section: Can I use the previous OTP after regenerating the DC?
text: No.

text: No. Once OTP authentication succeeds, the DC cannot be changed.

section: Can I complete the visit without OTP authentication?
text: No. The DC must be authenticated before the visit can be completed.

text: No.

Pickup means collecting used linen from a hotel for washing and cleaning.
Delivery means fresh linen delivered to the hotel.
Pickup means used or soiled linen collected from the hotel.
The driver performs pickup segregation at the hotel.
The driver is responsible for identifying and logging Heavy Soil and Damaged pickup items.

Pickup quantity means the actual quantity of linen collected from the hotel.
Pickup quantity usually matches the delivery quantity, but it does not have to match.
Example:
- Delivered quantity: 500 bath towels
- Actual pickup quantity: 480 bath towels
- Driver should enter pickup quantity as 480.
The driver does not have to enter the original delivery quantity as the pickup quantity.
The app allows the actual pickup quantity to be lower than the delivery quantity.
Remarks are optional. The driver may use Remarks to explain a quantity mismatch or another
unusual situation.

Heavy Soil means linen with heavy stains or dirt that cannot normally be cleaned through a
regular wash and requires special treatment.
Examples of Heavy Soil:
- Curry stain
- Blood stain
- Dried stain
- Set-in stain
- Grease mark
- Heavy dirt
- Heavy grime
- Any stain requiring special treatment
Simple rule:​
Heavy Soil is a stain or dirt problem requiring special treatment.

Damaged means linen with physical or structural damage.
Examples of Damaged linen:
- Torn linen
- Ripped linen
- Hole in the fabric
- Linen ripped in half
- Severely deteriorated fabric
- Physical defect that makes the linen unusable
Simple rule:​
Damaged is a physical or structural problem with the linen.

Heavy Soil is related to stains or dirt.
Damaged is related to physical damage.
Curry stain = Heavy Soil.
Blood stain = Heavy Soil.
Grease mark = Heavy Soil.
Dried stain = Heavy Soil.
Torn edge = Damaged.
Hole = Damaged.
Ripped linen = Damaged.
Ripped in half = Damaged.
Severely deteriorated fabric = Damaged.
Fading or discoloration by itself is not considered physical damage.

section: Linen With Both Heavy Soil and Damage
text:
A single linen unit can have both Heavy Soil and Damage.
Example:​
A bedsheet has a blood stain and a tear.
The driver must log the unit under Heavy Soil.
The driver must also log the unit under Damaged.
Heavy Soil and Damaged must be entered separately.
When one unit is logged under both Heavy Soil and Damaged, two photos are required.
One photo is required for the Heavy Soil entry.
One photo is required for the Damaged entry.

Heavy Soil and Damaged segregation must be performed at the hotel.
The driver performs the segregation at the hotel during the pickup visit.
The driver must complete the required pickup segregation and photos before leaving the hotel.
The driver cannot leave the hotel and complete the required photos later.

To enter pickup information:
1.​ Open the hotel visit.
2.​ Open the relevant order.
3.​ Tap Start Visit.
4.​ Start Visit can be performed only inside the hotel perimeter.
5.​ Open the Pickup tab.
6.​ Select the relevant product.
7.​ Select Heavy Soil or Damaged when applicable.
8.​ Enter the quantity.
9.​ Capture the required photo.
10.​Complete all required entries.
11.​Tap Save and Continue.

The quantity entered as Heavy Soil or Damaged cannot exceed the pickup quantity.
Example:​
Pickup quantity = 10 bath towels.
The driver cannot enter:
- 11 Heavy Soil bath towels
- 12 Damaged bath towels
The app prevents the driver from entering a Heavy Soil or Damaged quantity greater than the
pickup quantity.

A photo is mandatory for every flagged unit.
One Heavy Soil unit requires one Heavy Soil photo.
One Damaged unit requires one Damaged photo.
Examples:
5 damaged bath towels = 5 photos.
10 Heavy Soil bath towels = 10 photos.
3 damaged bedsheets = 3 photos.
7 Heavy Soil pillow covers = 7 photos.

The photo format is handled automatically by the Pushpak app.
The driver does not need to select a photo format.
The driver only needs to capture the picture through the app.

If a driver captures an incorrect, blurry, or unsuitable photo, the driver can remove the photo and
capture another one.
To remove a captured photo, tap the X button on the image.
After removing the image, the driver can capture a new photo.

Required photos must be captured at the hotel.
Photos cannot be uploaded after the driver leaves the hotel perimeter.
The driver must complete the required photos before proceeding to the next step.

The app blocks the driver from continuing when required photos have not been completed.
The driver cannot move to the next step until all required photos are captured.
The driver cannot leave the hotel and upload the missing photos later.

If the hotel disputes a Heavy Soil or Damaged classification, the driver should contact the team.
The driver should contact the team when the hotel disagrees with the classification of an item.

The driver is responsible for Heavy Soil and Damaged segregation because segregation
happens at the hotel.
The driver is responsible for:
- Identifying Heavy Soil.
- Identifying Damaged linen.
- Entering the relevant quantities.
- Capturing the required photos.
- Completing the pickup entry before leaving the hotel.

Remarks are optional.
Remarks can be used to explain:
- Pickup quantity mismatch.
- Unusual pickup situations.
- Other relevant information.
Remarks are not mandatory for every pickup.
Pickup is the collection of used linen from a hotel for washing and cleaning.

Heavy Soil is linen with heavy stains or dirt that requires special treatment because a normal
wash cannot clean it.

section: Is blood a Heavy Soil item?
text: Yes. Blood stains are Heavy Soil.

section: Is curry a Heavy Soil item?
text: Yes. Curry stains are Heavy Soil.
Yes. Heavy grease marks are Heavy Soil.

Damaged means linen with physical or structural damage such as tears, rips, holes, or severe
deterioration.
Yes. A torn towel is Damaged.
Yes. A hole is Damaged.
No. Fading or discoloration by itself is not physical damage.

section: What if linen has both a stain and a tear?
text:
Log the linen under both Heavy Soil and Damaged separately.
Two photos are required for the same unit: one for Heavy Soil and one for Damaged.

section: How many photos are required for 5 damaged towels?
text: 5 photos.

section: How many photos are required for 10 Heavy Soil towels?
text: 10 photos.

section: Can I skip the photo for a small amount of damage?
text: No. A photo is mandatory for every flagged unit.

section: Can I upload photos after leaving the hotel?
text: No. Required photos must be captured at the hotel.

section: Can I continue without taking all required photos?
text: No. The app blocks the driver from proceeding until all required photos are completed.
Yes. Tap the X button on the captured image to remove it and then capture a new photo.

section: Do I need to select the photo format?
text: No. The Pushpak app handles the photo format automatically.

section: Can Heavy Soil or Damaged quantity exceed pickup quantity?
text:
No. The app prevents entering a Heavy Soil or Damaged quantity greater than the pickup
quantity.

section: What if the hotel disputes a Heavy Soil or Damaged classification?
text: Contact the team.

section: Do pickup and delivery quantities have to match?
text: No. They usually match, but the driver should enter the actual pickup quantity.

section: What if 500 towels were delivered but only 480 are picked up?
text: Enter 480 as the pickup quantity. Remarks are optional.

section: Who performs Heavy Soil and Damaged segregation?
text: The driver performs the segregation at the hotel.

A Trip is a collection of multiple hotels that a driver is assigned to visit along a route.
One Trip can contain multiple hotels.
Each hotel in a Trip can have different:
- Linen types
- Quantities
- Contacts
- Delivery requirements
- Pickup requirements
A Trip is different from a Visit.
Trip = multiple hotels on a route.
Visit = work performed at one hotel.

A Visit is the work performed at one specific hotel during a Trip.
Each hotel in a Trip has its own Visit.
A Visit can include:
- Delivery
- Return Fresh
- Pickup
- Heavy Soil
- Damaged
- Remarks
- Digital DC
- OTP authentication
A Visit starts when the driver starts the visit at the hotel.

Trip

warehouse

| Trip | Visit |
|---|---|
| Contains multiple hotels | Represents one hotel |
| Covers the complete route | Covers work at one hotel |
| Started when exiting the warehouse | Started at the hotel |
| Contains multiple visits | Contains one hotel's delivery/pickup work |
| Ends after all hotels are completed | Completed after the hotel's required process is completed |

The driver receives assigned Trips in Pushpak.
Trips are available to the driver the same morning.
The driver should open the Pushpak app at the warehouse and refresh the app.
Refreshing the app is recommended but not mandatory.

Start Trip marks the beginning of the driver's Trip.
Start Trip can only be started when the driver is exiting the warehouse.
The driver cannot start the Trip from another location.
The Start Trip button is disabled when the driver is not at the required warehouse-exit location.
Starting the Trip indicates that the driver has started the route with the assigned load.

- Start Trip is only for the beginning of the Trip.
- Start Trip should be tapped when exiting the warehouse.
- Start Trip cannot be started from another location.
- The Start Trip button is disabled when it cannot be started.

A Trip contains a list of hotels.
Hotels are shown in a suggested visiting order.
The driver is completely free to choose the visiting order.
The driver does not have to visit hotels in numerical order.
Example:
Hotel 1 → Hotel 2 → Hotel 3 → Hotel 4
The driver can instead visit:
Hotel 1 → Hotel 3 → Hotel 4 → Hotel 2
The visiting order can be changed based on the driver's route and situation.

Start Visit begins the work for a specific hotel.
Start Visit can only be performed when the driver is inside the hotel's required perimeter.
The confirmed hotel perimeter is 2 meters.
If the driver is outside the hotel perimeter:
- Start Visit is completely blocked.
- The driver cannot start the Visit.
When the driver enters the required perimeter:
- Start Visit becomes available automatically.
- The driver does not need to refresh the app.

1.​ Driver arrives at the hotel.
2.​ Driver enters the required hotel perimeter.
3.​ Start Visit becomes available automatically.
4.​ Driver opens the hotel.
5.​ Driver opens the relevant order.
6.​ Driver taps Start Visit.
7.​ Hotel visit process begins.

The driver must be within the 2-meter hotel perimeter to start the Visit.
If the driver is outside the perimeter, the app completely blocks Start Visit.
The driver does not need to refresh after entering the perimeter because the availability updates
automatically.

Pushpak currently uses Regular Orders.
Regular Orders are scheduled hotel orders.
Regular Orders can be recurring based on the hotel's schedule.
Regular Orders can contain the hotel's delivery and pickup requirements.
The driver selects the relevant Regular Order when starting the hotel Visit.

Ad Hoc Orders are currently not in use in Pushpak.
The current Pushpak process uses Regular Orders.

A hotel can mostly have multiple Regular Orders in the same Visit.
The exact behavior for every possible multiple-order scenario is not further specified.

A driver can skip a hotel in the Trip.
If a hotel is skipped:
- The hotel remains Pending.
- The driver can continue with other hotels.
- The skipped hotel remains incomplete.

A skipped hotel remains in a Pending state.
A Pending hotel has not been completed.
A Pending hotel does not count as a completed Visit.

If the driver reaches a hotel and the hotel is:
- Closed
- Inaccessible
- Otherwise unavailable for the Visit
the driver should contact the team.
If there is no network at the hotel, the driver should contact the team.

Pushpak has an End Trip button.
The driver can tap End Trip only after all hotels in the Trip have been completed.
The End Trip button cannot be used while there are incomplete hotels.
The driver must complete the required hotel Visits before End Trip becomes available.

A Trip is considered complete when all hotels in the Trip have been completed.
The driver can then use the End Trip button.
The End Trip button cannot be tapped before all hotels are completed.

A Trip can still be completed when a hotel has a pending pickup.
The exact handling of the pending pickup after Trip completion is not further specified.

Trip reassignment is mostly not allowed.

specified.

The driver receives assigned Trips.
The exact internal method used to assign Trips is not required for the driver-facing knowledge

Recommended morning routine:
1.​ Reach the warehouse.
2.​ Open Pushpak.
3.​ Refresh the app.
4.​ View the assigned Trips.
5.​ Open the required Trip.
6.​ Review the hotels.
7.​ Exit the warehouse.
8.​ Tap Start Trip.
Refreshing is recommended but not mandatory.

The general Trip flow is:
1.​ Driver receives the Trip.
2.​ Driver reaches the warehouse.
3.​ Driver opens Pushpak.
4.​ Driver refreshes the app.
5.​ Driver reviews the assigned Trip.
6.​ Driver exits the warehouse.
7.​ Driver taps Start Trip.
8.​ Driver travels to the assigned hotels.
9.​ Driver can choose the hotel visiting order.
10.​Driver enters the required hotel perimeter.
11.​Start Visit becomes available automatically.
12.​Driver opens the hotel order.
13.​Driver taps Start Visit.
14.​Driver completes the hotel Visit.
15.​Driver repeats the process for other hotels.
16.​Any skipped hotel remains Pending.
17.​Once all hotels are completed, End Trip becomes available.
18.​Driver taps End Trip.
